Prepare Marker Panel Data for Whole-Genome Analysis for gwasAim and gpAim

Source: R/primePanel.R
primePanel.Rd

Converts a matrix or data frame of marker genotypes and an associated genetic map into a "wgPanel" object suitable for use with gwasAim and gpAim.

Usage

primePanel(
  geno,
  map,
  id = "id",
  map.id = "marker",
  map.chr = "chr",
  map.pos = "pos",
  encoding = "012",
  impute = "none",
  knn.k = 5L
)

Arguments

geno

A numeric matrix (lines x markers) with row names identifying lines, or a data.frame with a column named by id identifying lines and remaining columns containing marker genotypes.

Genotype values: The function accepts both integer-coded genotypes (0, 1, 2) and fractional dosage values in the range \([0, 2]\) output by imputation software such as Beagle, IMPUTE2, or Minimac. Under encoding = "012", the transformation \(x \mapsto x - 1\) is applied to all values whether or not they are integers, yielding dosage values in \([-1, 1]\). A pre-imputed dosage matrix therefore requires no further imputation inside primePanel.

map

A data.frame containing the genetic map with at minimum three columns: marker names (map.id), chromosome identifiers (map.chr), and cM positions (map.pos). Markers present in geno but absent from map are dropped with a message. Markers are sorted by position within each chromosome.

id

Character string naming the line identifier column in geno when geno is a data.frame. Ignored when geno is a matrix (row names are used). Default "id".

map.id

Character string naming the marker column in map. Default "marker".

map.chr

Character string naming the chromosome column in map. Default "chr". Chromosome names containing dots are replaced with underscores with a warning, as dots are used as field separators in internal marker naming.

map.pos

Character string naming the cM position column in map. Default "pos".

encoding

Character string specifying the genotype encoding in geno:

"012" (default)

Allele-count coding where 0 = AA homozygote, 1 = AB heterozygote, 2 = BB homozygote. Values are shifted by \(-1\) to produce additive \(\pm 1\) coding. This also accepts fractional dosage values in \([0, 2]\) output by imputation software – no additional handling is required.

"pm1"

Genotypes already in additive \(\pm 1\) coding. No transformation is applied. Fractional values in \([-1, 1]\) are accepted.

impute

Character string controlling how missing values (NA) are handled after encoding:

"none" (default)

No imputation is performed. If any NAs remain, primePanel stops with an informative error recommending pre-imputation with dedicated software. This is the recommended path for large panels.

"knn"

Chromosome-wise k-nearest neighbour imputation. For each chromosome the pairwise distance matrix is computed via tcrossprod() (BLAS), the neighbour ranking is pre-sorted once, and each missing value is imputed from the mean of the knn.k nearest lines that carry a non-missing call at that marker. Imputation respects linkage disequilibrium within each chromosome and is the recommended in-package option when pre-imputation with dedicated software is not feasible.

"mean"

Missing values are replaced with the column mean (mean genotype across lines at each marker). This is a crude approximation that ignores linkage disequilibrium and haplotype structure; it is provided only as a convenience for small panels or exploratory analyses. A warning is always issued when this option is used.

knn.k

Positive integer. Number of nearest neighbours used when impute = "knn". Default 5. Larger values produce smoother imputations but are slower; values between 3 and 10 are typical. Ignored when impute != "knn".

Value

An object of class c("wgPanel", "wgCross") – a list with:

$pheno

A data.frame with the line identifier column.

$geno

A named list (one element per chromosome) each containing:

$data

Encoded genotype matrix (lines x markers).

$map

Named numeric vector of cM positions.

$imputed.data

The analysis-ready genotype matrix (same as $data after any imputation) in additive \(\pm 1\) or dosage coding.

Details

Data quality and filtering:

primePanel assumes the data are already clean and ready for analysis. No MAF filtering, missingness filtering, or duplicate removal is performed. Use checkPanel to diagnose data quality issues and filterPanel to apply filters before calling primePanel. Alternatively, the filteredPanel S3 method accepts the output of filterPanel directly.

Missing data and imputation:

For real association panels, missing genotypes should be imputed using dedicated software before calling primePanel. Tools such as Beagle (https://faculty.washington.edu/browning/beagle/beagle.html), IMPUTE2, or Minimac use haplotype reference panels and linkage disequilibrium information to produce well-calibrated dosage values. Their output can be supplied directly to primePanel as a matrix of dosage values in \([0, 2]\) with encoding = "012" and impute = "none".

Column-mean imputation (impute = "mean") inflates apparent precision and ignores the LD structure that makes imputation informative. For a panel of \(n\) lines and \(p\) markers it requires \(O(np)\) operations and is fast, but the quality of imputed values degrades rapidly as missingness increases. It is not recommended for missing rates above 1–2%.

Encoding and dosage values:

The \(x \mapsto x - 1\) transformation under encoding = "012" is exact for integers and valid for fractional dosages. A dosage of 0.8 (likely heterozygous allele) becomes \(-0.2\); a dosage of 1.6 (likely BB) becomes \(+0.6\). Values are not rounded or thresholded; the full dosage information is preserved for use in the relationship matrix or marker effect model.

See also

gwasAim, gpAim, primeCross

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# --- Recommended path: check, filter, then prime with KNN imputation ---
chk   <- checkPanel(geno.mat, map.df)
print(chk)
clean <- filterPanel(chk, maf = 0.05, miss.line = 0.20, miss.marker = 0.20)
panel <- primePanel(clean, impute = "knn", knn.k = 5)

# --- Direct path (data already clean, no imputation needed) ---
panel <- primePanel(geno.mat, map.df, encoding = "012", impute = "none")

# --- KNN imputation on raw data ---
panel <- primePanel(geno.mat, map.df, encoding = "012",
                    impute = "knn", knn.k = 5)

# --- Mean imputation for quick exploratory analysis ---
panel <- primePanel(geno.mat, map.df, encoding = "012", impute = "mean")
} # }
